title: Non-null assertion on potentially missing DOM element
reasoning: The code uses a non-null assertion operator (!) on document.getElementById('root'), which can return null if the element doesn't exist. If the root element is missing from the HTML, this will throw a runtime error that crashes the entire application during initialization. This is a common issue in React applications where the HTML template might be misconfigured or the element ID mismatches.
reproduction: Load the application with an HTML file that doesn't contain a <div id='root'> element. The app will crash with 'Cannot read properties of null' error.
recommendation: Add a null check before calling createRoot. If the element is missing, provide a fallback error message or throw a descriptive error. Example: const rootElement = document.getElementById('root'); if (!rootElement) throw new Error('Root element not found'); ReactDOM.createRoot(rootElement).render(...)
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included in this feature. The feature metadata shows an empty tests array, so there's no test coverage for application initialization or DOM mounting.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that verifies graceful handling when the root element is missing: 1) Create a test HTML without #root, 2) Attempt to initialize the app, 3) Assert a descriptive error is thrown rather than a cryptic null reference error.
